intent: The catch-all Bedrock plugin that exposes raw SQL as a command: clients send a Query request and get back the result formatted per sqlite3-CLI-style flags or as JSON, with named bound parameters.

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_DB
objects.role: the plugin; recognizes Query requests and hands them to BedrockDBCommand

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_DB::Sqlite3QRFSpecWrapper
objects.role: move-only RAII wrapper owning the heap strings a sqlite3_qrf_spec's char pointers point into

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_DB::parseSQLite3Args
objects.role: parses sqlite3-CLI-style flags (-json, -csv, -separator, etc.) into a Sqlite3QRFSpecWrapper

objects.name: BedrockPlugin_DB::generateErrorContextMessage
objects.role: builds a two-line, caret-pointing error snippet mimicking the sqlite3 CLI's error display

objects.name: BedrockDBCommand
objects.role: BedrockCommand implementing peek()/process() for arbitrary read/write SQL with named bound parameters from sql-param-<name> headers

objects.name: BedrockDBCommand::SQLiteFormatAppend
objects.role: write callback registered with the QRF formatter to accumulate output

misfits.why: a generic sqlite3-CLI argument-parsing and error-formatting layer around libstuff/qrf.h's C struct, none of it specific to being a request-command plugin
misfits.suggested_home: libstuff/qrf.h or a new libstuff unit alongside it

name_fit.note: fits by convention as the original catch-all query plugin, though 'DB' alone doesn't convey that scope since every plugin touches the DB

naming_quality.note: Sqlite3QRFSpecWrapper's mixed casing matches the wrapped C API; depends on libstuff/SQliteParameter whose 'SQlite' capitalization is inconsistent with this codebase's usual 'SQLite'
